queries.query: ("data provenance" OR "artifact availability" OR reproducib* OR "open dataset" OR "benchmarks" OR GitHub OR Zenodo) AND (NetOps OR "network configuration" OR AIOps)
queries.rationale: Locate open datasets, reproducible artifacts, and provenance practices to support experiment reproducibility and verification.
source_preferences: Data repositories (GitHub, Zenodo, IEEE DataPort), benchmarks' official project pages

inclusion_criteria: Works that explicitly connect LLMs/LLM-based agents to network operations, configuration generation, or network-management automation.
Papers describing validators, formal verification, or deterministic analyzers for network configurations (NetKAT, Veriflow, HSA, etc.).
Empirical studies, case studies, benchmarks, surveys, and reproducible artifacts (code/datasets) with verifiable provenance.
Safety, security, and failure-analysis literature relevant to autonomous agents applied to critical network infrastructure.
Methodology and experimental-design papers discussing evaluation metrics, simulators/emulators (Mininet, ns-3), or measurement protocols.
Publicly accessible sources: peer-reviewed publications, preprints on arXiv, verifiable technical reports, and open repositories.
exclusion_criteria: Standalone LLM benchmarking that tests only factual/encyclopedic knowledge without operational NetOps tasks or validators.
Unverifiable blog posts, social-media threads, or marketing fluff without reproducible data or citations.
Proprietary internal incident reports or datasets that are not publicly accessible or lack verifiable artifacts.
Works outside the NetOps/AIOps domain unless they offer generalizable methods (e.g., formal verifier techniques) explicitly transferable to networking.
Pre-lock internal development artifacts or rehearsals not published or publicly available (per programme constraints).
Papers older than foundational verification works when superseded by more relevant modern treatments—except when explicitly foundational.
date_rationale: Prioritize literature from 2020–2026 for LLM-specific phenomena and mitigation research (post-transformer/ChatGPT era). Include earlier foundational networking verification and AIOps works (2005–2019) where they introduce enduring formal methods or testbeds (e.g., NetKAT, Veriflow, HSA, Anteater). This window balances recency for LLM developments with older, essential verification literature needed to build valid NetOps validators and benchmarks.
